intro: Barbers build loyal clients through conversation, skill and steady service. The closest of the 25 careers below is locker room and dressing room attending, with a 71% match, but better-paid options include Opticians, Dispensing at a 68% match and a BLS May 2025 median of $47,260, which is 24% more than the $38,210 barbers earn.
why_it_works: A day in the chair means reading what each client wants, keeping conversation easy and finishing on time for the next booking. O*NET rates social perceptiveness at 3.12 out of 5 for barbers, and service orientation and judgment at 2.88. Eyewear, spa and funeral service work use the same client care. All 25 matches need no extra education. The gaps are problem solving and teaching.
tips: Embalmers earn $58,780, which is 54% more, after a mortuary science program.
Transportation Security Screeners earn $66,770, or 75% more, and train new hires.
If you own a shop, spa management is a 68% match with a median of $69,770 for its broader group.

faq.q: What jobs can former barbers do?
faq.a: The closest matches are locker room and dressing room attendants (71%), maids and housekeeping cleaners (70%) and Bartenders (69%), based on O*NET 31.0. Dispensing opticians are 68% matched and earn $47,260, which is 24% more than the $38,210 barber median.

faq.q: Which careers for barbers pay more?
faq.a: 11 of the 25 matches pay more. Funeral Home Managers earn $78,790 (106% more), Transportation Security Screeners $66,770 (75% more) and Embalmers $58,780 (54% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Funeral service roles usually need a state license.

faq.q: Do barbers need more education to switch?
faq.a: No. All 25 matches need no more education than barbers already have, including all of the top 10. In the closest match, 64% of workers have a high school diploma or the equivalent, though some jobs, such as embalming, need a license.

The skills that most often need work are complex problem solving, coordination, instructing and time management. Judgment already rates 2.88 out of 5 for barbers in O*NET, so running a business or training others is the main step toward higher income.
